approach.label: Approach
approach.h2: Prototype early. Evaluate before autonomy. Hand it over.
approach.lead: A working agent is worth a thousand slides. I get to one fast, then make it boring enough to trust in production.

steps.label: 01 · Discover
steps.title: Find the workflow
steps.p: One to two weeks on your process and data. We pick the workflow worth automating, the success metric, and where a human stays in the loop.

steps.label: 02 · Prototype
steps.title: Prove it on real work
steps.p: A working agent on your actual documents and tools within weeks. Decide to continue on evidence, not a deck.

steps.label: 03 · Harden
steps.title: Earn the autonomy
steps.p: Evaluation suites, guardrails, observability and cost controls. Deployed on your cloud, integrated into the tools people already use.

steps.label: 04 · Hand over
steps.title: Your team owns it
steps.p: Documentation, training and a clean handover. The goal is a system you run without me, and a reason to call again.

principles.title: Evaluation before autonomy
principles.p: An agent gets more freedom only as the evals prove it deserves it. Measured, not assumed.

principles.title: Your stack, your cloud
principles.p: AWS, Databricks, GCP or Azure. No new vendor lock-in, and nothing that leaves your environment.

principles.title: No black boxes
principles.p: Readable code, documented decisions and evaluation you can rerun. You should be able to audit everything.

about.label: About
bio: I'm Berke, a Berlin-based AI consultant focused on agentic systems. I work at the intersection of applied research and delivery: comfortable reading the paper, but judged on whether the system runs in production and moves a business metric.

Since 2023 I have run the AI and GenAI portfolio at BeeBI Consulting for EU and US customers, from presales through post-deployment across five concurrent clients. Before that I was an early team member at TAZI AI through 4× growth and a $4.6M round, packaging its AI solutions into repeatable offerings and shipping retention, NLP and clinical models for US and European clients.

My master's research at Boğaziçi University on biomedical entity normalization with LLMs was published at the BioCreative VIII SympTEMIST track. An industrial engineering and economics double major at Koç University taught me to treat ML problems as business problems first.
I work in English and Turkish, and speak good German.
